brief: Distribution before product — 6 founders who built an audience before writing a line of code.

slots.subtitle: Six founders who captured demand before shipping a single feature, and how to repeat their playbook.
slots.preview1: How a newsletter became a $4M SaaS before beta
slots.preview2: The Twitter thread that pre-sold nine hundred seats
slots.preview3: Why community is cheaper than cold ads

slots.title: Write weekly,
slots.subtitle: A financial blogger turned his email list into a tax-tool startup.
slots.insight1Body: He sent 144 issues before sketching a single wireframe.
slots.insight2Body: The most-clicked link revealed the exact feature to build first.
slots.insight3Body: Pre-orders funded the first engineer within forty-eight hours.
slots.pullQuote: Your audience is the only moat that compounds faster than code.

slots.title: One viral thread,
slots.subtitle: A designer used a single tweetstorm to validate a cohort-based course.
slots.insight1Body: She shared Figma files daily for ninety days before building the curriculum.
slots.insight2Body: Personal replies turned lurkers into a waitlist of eager buyers.
slots.insight3Body: The thread focused on outcomes, not features, to drive pre-sales.
slots.pullQuote: Distribution is not a post-launch chore; it is the product you build first.

slots.title: Community first,
slots.subtitle: A founder ran a paid Slack group that became the roadmap for his CRM.
slots.insight1Body: A $5 monthly gate filtered out freebie hunters and surfaced real buyers.
slots.insight2Body: Support threads became a spec sheet no agency could have written.
slots.insight3Body: The first one hundred users came from inside the community walls.
slots.pullQuote: If they won't pay for the community, they won't pay for the software.

slots.title: Show your work,
slots.subtitle: A developer live-streamed bug fixes until his audience begged for his IDE plugin.
slots.insight1Body: Raw debugging sessions outperformed polished tutorials three to one.
slots.insight2Body: Viewers typed the exact UI complaints that shaped the final design.
slots.insight3Body: A simple Typeform in the bio captured ten thousand emails in two weeks.
slots.pullQuote: People don't buy tools; they buy the person who taught them how to use them.

slots.title: Interview buyers,
slots.subtitle: A podcast host recorded fifty calls before launching a talent marketplace.
slots.insight1Body: Every interview was a user research session disguised as content.
slots.insight2Body: Blog posts from calls ranked on Google before the product existed.
slots.insight3Body: Guests introduced their networks, building supply before demand.
slots.pullQuote: The best MVP is a microphone and a calendar full of strangers.

slots.title: Consult first,
slots.subtitle: A LinkedIn creator sold services until a repeatable playbook became software.
slots.insight1Body: Agency work funded development and proved the workflow was valuable.
slots.insight2Body: Checklists built for interns became the feature set of the final app.
slots.insight3Body: Clients were offered lifetime deals before the beta was even live.
slots.pullQuote: Revenue from services is the only market validation that pays your rent.

slots.ctaBody: Audience-first founders win because distribution compounds while code depreciates. Build the crowd before the castle.
